s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute pulmonary syndrome in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: Bilateral diffuse alveolar infiltrates on chest radiograph
Bilateral diffuse ground-glass opacities on high-resolution CT
Positive Pneumocystis jirovecii on Grocott’s methenamine silver stain
New left upper-zone infiltrates after discontinuation of TMP-SMX
key_facts: 36-year-old man with end-stage renal disease secondary to IgA nephropathy
Underwent live-related renal transplant 6 months ago
Maintained on tacrolimus, mycophenolate sodium, and prednisolone
Presented with 14-day history of low-grade fever, dry cough, and anorexia
Afebrile on admission with heart rate 88 beats/min and blood pressure 122/76 mm Hg
Respiratory rate 28 breaths/min and oxygen saturation 95% on room air
Bilateral inspiratory crackles on examination
Hemoglobin 14.6 g/dL, total lymphocyte count 9900/μL, and absolute neutrophil count 7720/μL
Arterial blood gas analysis showed PaO₂ 68 mm Hg and an A–a gradient of 22 mm Hg
HIV ELISA was negative
Sputum induction was non-diagnostic
Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid was positive for Pneumocystis jirovecii
Treated with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and a prednisone taper
Leukopenia developed after discontinuation of TMP-SMX
New left upper-zone infiltrates and patchy peribronchovascular consolidations on repeat HRCT

shortlist.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Positive BAL fluid result and response to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole

shortlist.label: Cytomegalovirus pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised state and subacute pulmonary syndrome

shortlist.label: Invasive aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised state and new infiltrates after discontinuation of TMP-SMX

shortlist.label: Idiopathic pneumonia syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Subacute pulmonary syndrome and lack of diagnostic findings for other infections

shortlist.label: Pulmonary nocardiosis
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised state and new patchy peribronchovascular consolidations on repeat HRCT

raw.rationale: The patient's diagnosis is supported by the presence of Pneumocystis jirovecii in the bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, which is a definitive diagnostic finding, and the clinical and radiographic resolution of infiltrates after treatment with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole

rejected.label: Cytomegalovirus pneumonia
rejected.why: CMV inclusion bodies were not found in the BAL fluid

rejected.label: Invasive aspergillosis
rejected.why: Fungal hyphae were not found in the BAL fluid

rejected.label: Pulmonary nocardiosis
rejected.why: There is no mention of Nocardia species in the diagnostic findings
